# External Documents Runbook — SBA E2G (SB-GC7J-26-001)

**Purpose.** This runbook covers the three application attachments that cannot be generated by Mimir Labs internally — they are either real artifacts produced by external parties, real biographical content for real people, or formal elections that require organizational sign-off. Each section below tells you (a) what the document is, (b) whether E2G actually requires it for Mimir Labs, (c) how to acquire or compose it, (d) the required content and format, and (e) timeline and contact points.

**Opportunity.** SBA Empower to Grow (E2G) Program — Manufacturing track, FY2026. Solicitation **SB-GC7J-26-001**. Announced May 6, 2026. Application portal: grants.gov. Program inbox: e2g@sba.gov.

**Authoritative references** (cite these in any document you produce so the reviewer knows you read them):
- 2 CFR Part 200 — Uniform Administrative Requirements, Cost Principles, and Audit Requirements for Federal Awards (Uniform Guidance)
- 2 CFR 200.414 — Indirect (F&A) costs
- 2 CFR 200.414(f) — De minimis indirect cost rate
- 2 CFR 200 Subpart F — Audit Requirements (the Single Audit rule)
- 2 CFR 200 §§200.500–200.521 — Single Audit specifics
- SBA E2G NOFO (download from grants.gov listing 358669 once published; the FY25 NOFO under SB-GC7J-25-001 is the closest authoritative model until the FY26 NOFO posts)

## 1. Key Personnel Resumes

### What SBA wants

A federal grant resume is **not** a job-search resume. It is a structured CV that documents the named individual's capacity to perform the specific role they are committed to in the proposal. Reviewers use it to score "key personnel qualifications" — which on most SBA cooperative agreements is 15–25% of total points.

### Who counts as "key personnel"

Anyone listed in the **Key Personnel** section of the budget narrative who has named time commitment on the project. For E2G, this typically includes:

- **Project Director / Principal Investigator** — overall responsibility, named on cover page
- **Senior Technical Advisor(s)** — subject-matter leads (manufacturing, data, ERP)
- **Training / Curriculum Lead** — owns the TA delivery curriculum
- **Operations / Compliance Manager** — federal-grant compliance, reporting, audit liaison

If you list someone with ≥10% effort on the project, they need a resume. People with <10% effort can be described in a single paragraph in the narrative without a separate resume attachment.

### Required content (federal grant resume format)

Each resume must be **2–3 pages, no more**, in this order:

1. **Header**: Full legal name, position title, organization, contact email/phone.
2. **Position on this project**: One sentence stating the role, FTE percentage, and primary responsibilities under SB-GC7J-26-001. *Example: "Project Director (50% FTE) — overall scientific, technical, and administrative responsibility for the proposed work, including direct supervision of all subrecipient and consultant activity."*
3. **Education**: Degrees in reverse chronological order. Institution, degree, field, year.
4. **Professional experience**: Reverse chronological. For each position: organization, title, dates (month/year), one paragraph (3–6 lines) describing relevant scope, scale, outcomes. Quantify wherever possible — *"led 14-person delivery team," "managed $2.1M annual budget," "served 47 manufacturing clients."*
5. **Relevant qualifications**: A bulleted list of 5–8 specific qualifications that map to the work proposed under E2G. *Example: "Direct experience with ERP implementation in small-to-mid-market manufacturing environments (MRP II, BOM management, MES integration)."*
6. **Selected publications, presentations, products, or patents**: Only if directly relevant. List up to 10. For Mimir Labs, this is where the essay corpus, Yggdrasil ERP, and Mimisbrunnr framework should appear if the named person owns or co-owns them.
7. **Other support / current and pending**: Any other federal awards the individual is currently funded by, with title, role, period, total budget, person-months committed. **This is mandatory.** If none, write "*None — applicant has no prior or pending federal support.*" Misstating this is a finding-grade issue at audit.
8. **Certifications**: Any directly relevant credentials (PMP, CGFM, certified MEP, lean Six Sigma, etc.).

### Style and formatting

- 11 pt or 12 pt serif font, 1-inch margins, single-spaced, no graphics, no color, no photo.
- File format: PDF, one resume per file.
- File naming: `Resume_LastName_FirstName.pdf` (some federal agencies enforce this; SBA does not always, but it never hurts).
- Do not include personal information beyond business contact: no home address, no SSN, no DOB, no marital status, no photograph.

### How to compose for Mimir Labs key personnel

The minimum slate for E2G is one Project Director (Chris Gaither). Realistic full slate:

| Role | FTE % | Who | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Project Director | 40–60% | Chris Gaither | Resume must emphasize manufacturing-domain ERP design, multi-tenant data architecture, and any prior client-delivery scope (even pre-Mimir-Labs) |
| Senior Technical Advisor — Manufacturing | 15–30% | TBD or contracted SME | Real industry depth required; if in-house gap, name an external consultant with executed agreement |
| Training / Curriculum Lead | 15–25% | TBD | Adult-education or instructional-design background helpful; curriculum delivery is a scored capability |
| Operations / Compliance Manager | 10–20% | TBD or fractional | Must demonstrate federal-grant compliance experience or document a planned acquisition (fractional CFO with federal-grant exposure is a common pattern) |

**For roles where Mimir Labs does not currently have an internal candidate**, you have three options:

1. **Named consultant**: Contract an SME and attach the executed agreement (or LOI) plus their resume. Reviewers are accustomed to this.
2. **TBD / "to be hired"**: Reviewers will discount these heavily. Use only for roles where you can credibly hire post-award (project coordinator, junior trainer).
3. **Subrecipient**: Partner with an established TA-delivery org (MEP center, university extension, etc.) and have them name the personnel. Their resumes attach to your application as part of the subaward documentation.

### Timeline

Allocate **3–5 business days** per resume from initial draft to final PDF. The bottleneck is usually getting the named person to honestly populate the "current and pending support" and "selected publications" sections.

## 2. Single Audit

### What it is

A Single Audit (formerly OMB Circular A-133, now governed by 2 CFR 200 Subpart F) is a comprehensive audit of a non-federal entity's federal awards, performed by an independent CPA firm, covering financial statements and federal compliance. It produces a Schedule of Expenditures of Federal Awards (SEFA), a Schedule of Findings and Questioned Costs, and a final audit report submitted to the Federal Audit Clearinghouse.

### Whether Mimir Labs needs one

**You are required to have a Single Audit for any fiscal year in which you expended ≥ $750,000 of federal awards** (2 CFR 200.501(a)). "Expended" means actually spent down, not awarded.

**Mimir Labs threshold check** (verify each before answering):

| Test | Likely answer for Mimir Labs |
|---|---|
| Has Mimir Labs ever received a federal grant, cooperative agreement, or contract for which it was the prime recipient? | **No** (verify against SAM.gov entity record) |
| Has Mimir Labs ever been a subrecipient of pass-through federal funds? | **No** (verify against accounting records) |
| Has any single fiscal year of Mimir Labs's operating history seen federal expenditures ≥ $750K? | **No** |

If all three answers are "no," **a Single Audit is not required** and the application requirement is satisfied by submitting a brief memo on Mimir Labs letterhead stating so. Template:

> **MEMORANDUM**
>
> **TO:** SBA E2G Grants Management Officer
> **FROM:** [Authorized organizational representative]
> **DATE:** [Submission date]
> **RE:** Single Audit Status — SB-GC7J-26-001 Application
>
> Mimir Labs LLC has not been required to undergo a Single Audit pursuant to 2 CFR 200 Subpart F because, in no fiscal year of the organization's operating history, has Mimir Labs LLC expended federal awards meeting or exceeding the $750,000 threshold established at 2 CFR 200.501(a). Mimir Labs LLC has not been a prime recipient or subrecipient of federal financial assistance prior to this application.
>
> The applicant acknowledges and agrees that a Single Audit will be obtained for any fiscal year in which federal expenditures meet or exceed the threshold during the period of performance of any award resulting from this application.
>
> [Signature block: Name, title, date]

That memo, signed and dated, is the entire deliverable.

### If a Single Audit IS required

If any of the threshold-check answers are "yes" and you have not yet completed an audit, you cannot generate one for this application — only an independent CPA firm can. The path:

1. Engage a CPA firm with Single Audit experience (not all firms have it; ask explicitly). The American Institute of CPAs maintains a list of firms with Government Audit Quality Center membership.
2. Provide them with: prior-year financial statements, full federal award documentation, accounting records, prior audit reports if any, internal control documentation.
3. Audit fieldwork typically takes 6–12 weeks for a small entity; total engagement (planning through final report) typically 3–4 months.
4. Final report is filed with the Federal Audit Clearinghouse (FAC) at facweb.census.gov.
5. The FAC-stamped report is what you attach to the grant application.

If Mimir Labs has had federal funds I do not know about, **flag it immediately** — the application timeline does not accommodate originating a Single Audit from scratch.

## 3. Indirect Cost Rate Agreement / Extension Letter

### What it is

An indirect cost rate is the percentage of a recipient's indirect costs (overhead — rent, utilities, executive salaries, IT infrastructure not directly chargeable to a project) that the federal government will reimburse, expressed as a percentage of a defined direct cost base. The agreement formalizing this rate is called a **Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement (NICRA)**, and it is issued by the federal **cognizant agency** for the recipient (the federal agency that has historically provided the most direct funding, or HHS by default for most non-profits and small entities).

### Whether Mimir Labs has one

**Almost certainly no.** A NICRA is the result of a formal negotiation that takes 6–18 months and requires a meaningful federal-funding history. First-time federal applicants rarely have one. Confirm the absence by searching Mimir Labs's records for any document titled "Indirect Cost Rate Agreement" or correspondence from a federal cognizant agency on the topic.

### What to submit instead — three paths

#### Path A: 10% de minimis rate election (recommended)

Under **2 CFR 200.414(f)**, any non-federal entity that has never received a NICRA may elect to charge a flat 10% indirect cost rate against its **modified total direct costs** (MTDC). MTDC is defined at 2 CFR 200.1 — broadly, all direct salaries, fringe benefits, supplies, services, travel, and the first $25,000 of each subaward, excluding equipment, capital expenditures, hospitalization charges, rental costs, scholarships, and the portion of each subaward exceeding $25,000.

The election is submitted as a **letter on Mimir Labs letterhead**, signed by the authorized organizational representative. Template:

> **[Date]**
>
> SBA Grants Management Officer
> Empower to Grow Program
> U.S. Small Business Administration
> [Address from NOFO]
>
> **RE: De Minimis Indirect Cost Rate Election — SB-GC7J-26-001**
>
> Dear Grants Management Officer:
>
> Pursuant to 2 CFR 200.414(f), Mimir Labs LLC hereby elects to charge a de minimis indirect cost rate of ten percent (10%) of modified total direct costs (MTDC), as that base is defined at 2 CFR 200.1, against any award resulting from the above-referenced application. Mimir Labs LLC has never received a federally negotiated indirect cost rate agreement and is therefore eligible to make this election.
>
> Mimir Labs LLC commits to applying this rate consistently across all federal awards for the duration of the period of performance, or until such time as a Negotiated Indirect Cost Rate Agreement is executed with our cognizant federal agency.
>
> Sincerely,
>
> [Signature]
> [Name], [Title]
> Mimir Labs LLC
> UEI: [Mimir Labs UEI from SAM.gov]
>
> *(Note: I can produce the final version of this letter as a separate file once you confirm the authorized signatory and Mimir Labs's UEI.)*

That letter, signed and dated, is the indirect-cost-rate attachment. Done.

**Trade-off note:** 10% is a low rate. Established TA providers often run NICRAs in the 35–60% range. The de minimis election leaves real overhead reimbursement on the table. The trade is paid in exchange for not having to wait 12–18 months for a negotiated rate. For a first cooperative agreement, the trade is almost always correct.

#### Path B: Negotiate a NICRA with the cognizant agency

Only viable if Mimir Labs has already received federal funding sufficient to support a rate proposal. Process:

1. Determine the cognizant agency. For for-profit entities applying through SBA, the cognizant agency is typically the Defense Contract Audit Agency (DCAA) or HHS depending on funding history. Contact the SBA grants management office (e2g@sba.gov) for confirmation.
2. Prepare an indirect cost rate proposal package: certified financial statements, schedules of indirect costs and direct costs, allocation methodology, executive compensation justification, related-party disclosures.
3. Submit to the cognizant agency.
4. Wait 6–18 months for negotiation and issuance.

**Not feasible inside the FY26 application window.** Document only.

#### Path C: Extension letter (only if existing NICRA)

If you discover Mimir Labs has an existing NICRA (it does not, as far as I know, but verify), and the rate period covers the FY26 E2G award period, no action is required — attach a copy of the executed NICRA. If the existing NICRA is expiring before the period of performance ends, draft an extension request to the cognizant agency at least **90 days before expiration**, requesting a one-year extension under 2 CFR 200.414(g). The cognizant agency may issue an extension letter in lieu of a renegotiation. Attach the extension letter to the application.

### Which path to take for E2G FY26

**Path A (10% de minimis election).** Highest probability path, fastest, fully compliant, well-precedented for first-time federal applicants. The letter template above is the deliverable, customized with date, signatory, and UEI.

## Action checklist

Pre-submission, in order of urgency:

- [ ] **Confirm UEI active** (Mimir Labs has UEI per `business/UEI.pdf` — verify SAM.gov registration is current and not expired)
- [ ] **Confirm SAM.gov registration is active and complete** (cannot submit without this; renewal takes 7–10 business days if lapsed)
- [ ] **Verify Single Audit non-applicability** (confirm no prior federal funds via accounting records)
- [ ] **Identify and recruit named key personnel** (Project Director confirmed = Chris Gaither; identify or contract Senior Technical Advisor, Training Lead, Compliance Manager)
- [ ] **Compose key personnel resumes** (3–5 business days each, federal-format, 2–3 pages, with current/pending support disclosure)
- [ ] **Sign Single Audit "Not Applicable" memo** (or provide existing audit if applicable)
- [ ] **Sign 10% de minimis indirect cost election letter** (will be drafted to final once signatory and date confirmed)
- [ ] **File all six attachments per the application's List of Attachments** (drafted separately once final inventory locked)

## Common pitfalls

1. **Saying "to be hired" for too many key personnel.** Reviewers heavily discount unnamed personnel. Name them or partner with a subrecipient that has named them.
2. **Misstating "current and pending support" on a resume.** Federal investigators audit this. Honesty is non-negotiable, including on resumes for key personnel who have other jobs.
3. **Choosing a NICRA path when the de minimis is faster.** Some applicants over-engineer this and miss the deadline. The 10% election is fully compliant and routinely accepted.
4. **Submitting a "draft" memo for Single Audit non-applicability.** Sign and date it. An unsigned memo will be rejected as incomplete.
5. **Forgetting the SAM.gov "Representations & Certifications" annual update.** Lapsed reps and certs invalidate an otherwise valid SAM registration. Check during pre-submission.
6. **Missing the period-of-performance match between the indirect cost election and the proposed grant period.** The de minimis election letter must commit Mimir Labs to applying the rate "for the duration of the period of performance." If the proposed PoP is 36 months, the letter binds for 36 months.
